comparaison-01.why: The proportional structure Plus…, plus… (the more…, the more…), with no article in either part. le plus is the superlative; Autant… must pair with autant… and can’t go with plus.

comparaison-02.why: The proportional structure Moins…, moins… (the less…, the less…), with no article. le moins is the superlative; plus moins is a wrong combination.

comparaison-03.why: The fixed form for “more and more” is de plus en plus. plus en plus lacks de; de plus à plus doesn’t exist.

comparaison-04.why: The fixed form for “less and less” is de moins en moins, modifying the verb regardent. The other two options are wrongly formed.

comparaison-05.why: moindre is already a comparative; with an article it forms the superlative la moindre (the slightest), often in the negative: pas la moindre idée. You can’t add plus; le moindre doesn’t agree with the feminine noun idée.

comparaison-06.why: The comparative of mauvais can be pire (itself a comparative): pire qu’hier. plus pire doubles the comparison and is wrong; la pire is the superlative and can’t take que to compare with yesterday.

comparaison-07.why: The superlative la pire + noun (the worst decision), agreeing with the feminine noun décision. la plus pire is a wrong combination; le pire is masculine.

comparaison-08.why: d’autant plus que + indicative means “all the more… because…” (a reinforcing reason). autant plus lacks d’; de plus en plus expresses progression and can’t form a reason with que.

comparaison-09.why: d’autant plus + adjective + que + reason: I’m all the more disappointed because I had been promised a promotion. de plus en plus doesn’t introduce a reason with que; autant doesn’t modify adjectives (adjectives take aussi).

comparaison-10.why: The balanced contrast Autant…, autant… (on the one hand…, on the other…) uses autant in both halves. Tant and Plus don’t match the autant in the second half.

comparaison-11.why: comme si (as if) expresses a hypothetical comparison, with si elided before il: comme s’il connaissait. comme que doesn’t exist; tel que gives examples or means “such as” and can’t introduce this hypothesis.

comparaison-12.why: comme si takes the indicative imparfait for a simultaneous hypothesis contrary to reality: comme si elle était. si takes neither the conditional serait nor the subjunctive soit.

comparaison-13.why: comme si + plus-que-parfait means the hypothetical action happened before the main clause: comme s’il n’avait rien entendu. si takes neither the conditional aurait nor the subjunctive ait.

comparaison-14.why: tel que works as an adjective and agrees with the noun it refers to: les résultats (masculine plural) → tels. telles is feminine; tel is singular.

comparaison-15.why: tel que introduces examples and agrees with the preceding noun des pays (masculine plural): tels que. telles is feminine; tel is singular.

comparaison-16.why: tel que agrees with the preceding noun des villes (feminine plural): telles que. tels is masculine; telle is singular.

comparaison-17.why: The proportional structure Plus…, plus…: the two halves match, so the second also uses plus, with no article. le plus is the superlative; davantage can’t introduce the second half in this structure.

comparaison-18.why: au moindre + noun = “at the slightest…” (au moindre problème). moins is an adverb and can’t modify a noun directly; mineur is an ordinary adjective (minor), not used in this set phrase and placed after the noun.

comparaison-19.why: Comparing quantities of a noun takes autant de + noun + que. aussi only modifies adjectives and adverbs; tant de isn’t used in this que comparison (it can only replace autant in the negative).

comparaison-20.why: Comparing the degree of a verb takes autant que (Elle travaille autant que lui). aussi modifies adjectives or adverbs; si is only used for comparing adjectives in the negative.

comparaison-21.why: d’autant plus must pair with que: d’autant plus inquiet que…. car and parce que can’t form this fixed structure with d’autant plus.

comparaison-22.why: The proportional structure Plus…, plus…: the more the city spreads, the longer the commutes. mieux is the comparative of bien and can’t modify the adjective longs; autant doesn’t pair with plus.

comparaison-23.why: The superlative of bon is le meilleur / la meilleure (agreeing with solution). You don’t say la plus bonne; mieux is the comparative of the adverb bien and doesn’t modify nouns.

comparaison-24.why: Modifying the verb aller takes mieux, the comparative of the adverb bien (sales are doing better than last year). meilleur is an adjective; plus bien is wrong.

comparaison-25.why: The proportional structure Moins…, moins…: the less you exercise, the less you want to. le moins is the superlative; plus moins doesn’t exist.

comparaison-26.why: comme si + indicative imparfait: as if he were a millionaire. Neither the conditional serait nor the subjunctive soit can follow si.

comparaison-27.why: The fixed expression autant que possible (as much as possible). aussi que can’t be used on its own; tant que isn’t standard here.

comparaison-28.why: pas le moindre + noun (not the slightest…), agreeing with the masculine noun effort: le moindre. le moins is the superlative adverb and can’t modify a noun; la moindre is feminine.

comparaison-29.why: Comparing an adjective (performant) takes aussi… que. autant modifies verbs or takes de + noun; tant only replaces aussi / autant in the negative.

comparaison-30.why: d’autant moins que + reason: he had always supported the project, so I understand his decision all the less. de moins en moins expresses progression and doesn’t introduce a reason with que; autant moins lacks d’.
